title: Draft Ten Social Media Posts
description: Write ten original social media posts that communicate the brand's value proposition, explain relevant product features, address audience needs, and encourage meaningful engagement. Each post should have a distinct purpose and should be adapted to the communication style, content conventions, and audience expectations of its intended platform. The writing must be clear, compelling, audience-focused, and consistent with the approved brand voice. All product claims, feature descriptions, statistics, and other factual statements must be supported by approved product information rather than assumptions or invented details.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A claims register first: nothing enters a post that is not already sourced
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The brief's hardest rule is that every claim is supported, so build the register before the copy. Step 1: a one-row-per-fact register of everything the ten posts may say - feature, plan limit, price, audience statement - each with the source it comes from (a live zedu.chat page with the date checked, or an approved product document), and anything not in the register is off limits. Step 2: write the ten posts using only register rows, each tagged with the rows it used, so a reviewer can check a post in seconds. Step 3: a voice pass across all ten for one consistent person speaking, plus a platform-fit pass so the same message reads natively on each. Deliverables: the register, the ten posts with their row tags, and a short check note listing any claim that was cut because no source existed.

upvotes.reason: Grounding 'Draft Ten Social Media Posts' in verified operational workflows and empirical research accelerates adoption while preventing wasted feature churn.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Ten posts as one cohort's story, from setup to demo day
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A week of disconnected posts fades; a follow-along series gives readers a reason to come back. Approach: write the ten posts as the journey of one cohort - creating the workspace, the first Buzz class, sharing files, running an assignment thread, a mid-course check-in, demo day - each post opening with the moment that cohort is living that day and carrying one practical step a programme manager could copy tomorrow. Product facts are checked in the live app like every other approach here, and no outcome is claimed that the product can't show. Tasks: outline the story and check each beat against the app (research), write the ten posts (content).

upvotes.reason: "Ten posts as one cohort's story, from setup to demo day" has a scriptable structure, so it can be produced and reviewed rather than left open-ended. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Ten posts, each one operator question answered with a checked source
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build the ten posts around the questions cohort operators actually ask, so every post has one job and one checkable claim. Each post starts from a single question an operator has (where did the file go, why did learners go quiet, the same five questions again, who actually turned up), answers it in the platform's own format (LinkedIn as a short argument, X as one finding plus a link, Instagram as a five-slide walkthrough), and links to the Zedu page that backs the product claim, with the date checked. Hand over a posting sheet with the ten posts, the platform and format for each, the one action each post asks for, and the source line behind every product or number claim. No invented statistics: anything that cannot be checked is cut before the draft is shared.

upvotes.reason: "Ten posts, each one operator question answered with a checked source" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Ten posts, ten real screens: show the product, claim only what the screen proves
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A post people trust shows the thing working. Each of the ten posts is built around one screenshot taken from the live app on the day of writing - a channel with an announcement, a Buzz call in progress, a file shared into a channel, a thread reply - with two or three lines of copy that describe exactly what the picture shows and nothing beyond it. The screenshot is the claim check: if the copy says it, the image shows it, which is how the brief's 'no invented feature descriptions' is satisfied without a second review pass. Deliverables: ten post blocks (platform, image, caption, and a one-line note saying which screen was captured on which date), plus a list of the screens still needed if any cannot be captured. Screens are captured from a real workspace with no real student data in shot.

upvotes.reason: Grounding 'Draft Ten Social Media Posts' in verified operational workflows and empirical research accelerates adoption while preventing wasted feature churn.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Ten social posts, each one live-verified claim plus a fact-check column
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Approach: draft ten posts in plain educator language, one per core feature (Channels, DMs, Buzz, Files, Threads) plus two founder-style and three tip-style posts. Every post states exactly one claim that I verify in the signed-in app before writing, and ships with a fact-check column naming the route where it was checked. Why it fits: the goal's workstreams need posts that survive scrutiny and match the real product, not marketing guesses. Done: ten ready-to-post drafts + verification table, each under the platform's character limit. Measured: posts with a verified claim vs without, tracked against the existing 4% engagement goal; zero posts containing claims that cannot be traced to a live-app route.

rejectedIdeas.title: Ten product-moment posts: one real action in the app, proof in the frame
rejectedIdeas.description: Most feature posts say what the product does without showing it. Approach: pick ten real moments a course lead recognises - sending a Buzz invite, pinning a file to a thread, muting an announcement channel - and build one post per moment with the exact click path, a screenshot or short screen recording in the frame, and a one-line benefit in the audience's own words. Every claim comes from a live check on the day; anything not verifiable doesn't ship. Tasks: verify ten moments in the live app (research), write the ten posts (content).
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: Largely duplicates the accepted workstream 'ten real screens'; its example moments such as pinning a file or muting an announcement channel are not described on Zedu's public product pages, so they may not be shippable.
